source.title: The Master Key Hypothesis: Unlocking Cross-Model Capability Transfer via Linear Subspace Alignment
source.authors: R. Balasubramanian; Pin-Jie Lin; Rituraj Sharma; Anjie Fang; Fardin Abdi; Viktor Rozgic; Zhengyuan Du; Mohit Bansal; Tu Vu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model transfer using low-rank linear subspace alignment and downstream reasoning accuracy, rather than directly comparing the similarity of representations across scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports capability-transfer accuracy and some mapping reconstruction-error analyses. Its discussion of prior studies is not treated as evidence. The narrowing of generated opening words is not recorded as representation convergence: it measures output trajectories, not distances between representations. Extensive additional model, benchmark, hyperparameter, and figure results are omitted; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The paper relies on cross-model linear mappability as a tool. It extracts steering directions, maps them through a low-rank linear map, and reports downstream benchmark accuracy of its own method (Unlock). Accuracy gains after steering do not measure how well one model's representations align with or map onto another's. That is a steering effect with no measure of representational alignment. The one direct measure of mapping loss, the normalized L2 reconstruction error of the map (Figs 9-10), appears only as plots with trend descriptions. It is an in-sample fitting diagnostic of the method's own map. The text gives no readable values, and cross-model similarity is not compared across scale. The authors read the cross-family transfer as evidence of converging capability representations (App. D.2). That reading rests on steering accuracy, not on a representation measure, so no version verdict is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that capability directions can be extracted training-free and transferred across sizes, and preliminarily across families, via low-rank linear alignment. Gains are largest small-to-large and when the target holds the capability latently; transfer cannot add absent capabilities. They call cross-family results evidence of converging capability representations (citing the PRH), while stating this is empirical support, not mechanistic proof.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive activation directions, low-rank linear alignment, and inference-time steering, then evaluates downstream capability accuracy. It is not a direct reproduction of the original Platonic Representation Hypothesis distance-similarity method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with source/target transfer direction, model family and scale, task-conditioned versus task-agnostic data, benchmark, alignment rank, number of examples, and aggregator choice. The paper says neither mean nor PCA aggregation consistently wins.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive capability directions (CoT; base vs instruct math), mapped by a low-rank linear map, raise target accuracy within families and from Qwen1.5 to gemma-2/OLMo-2. Transfer is asymmetric: small-to-large gains more. Gains are weak where the target lacks the capability (gemma-2-2B, gemma-3). Some Qwen3 benchmark/regime combinations fall below baseline. Optimal rank, n and alpha differ per pair (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behaviour-inducing steering directions transfer across language models of different sizes and families through a low-rank linear alignment, eliciting latent capabilities in the target.

record.problems: Most central results are downstream accuracy rather than direct tests of representation-distance similarity or interchangeability loss. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates in the cited result tables. Hyperparameters are selected by grid search on held-out development data; the paper itself notes sensitivity to configuration. Some mapping-error trends are available only as plots, with qualitative descriptions in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted many separately reported CoT results from Qwen2.5, Qwen3, OLMo-2, and other gemma-2 configurations in Tables 1 and 4; additional mathematical-transfer configurations and checkpoints in Tables 6 and 7; and further mapping/steering settings in Appendix B and figures. Prioritised representative transfer directions, cross-family results, Qwen3 task-regime comparisons, weak or negative outcomes, and mapping sensitivity. These omitted results are not averaged or treated as evidence of direct representation-distance convergence.

untested.parts: No comparison of cross-model representational similarity as a function of scale or capability.

Only downstream steering accuracy and figure-only, in-sample reconstruction error of a low-rank map. No stated magnitude of mapping loss, no held-out reconstruction, no stitching, relative representations or unpaired mapping.
No identification of recurring features or circuits across models.
No alternative similarity metrics, neighbourhood settings, or out-of-distribution alignment comparisons. Rank/n sensitivity concerns the method's map fit.
No measure of how complete alignment is, whether it plateaus, or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

missing.what: Plotted normalized L2 mapping error per layer: roughly 0.1-0.3 for Qwen1.5 pairs, up to about 0.8 at some OLMo-2-7B<-1B layers. Approximate values could be read from the plots to show map loss magnitude per pair.

record.verdict_notes: Original-source check: not one of the originals. The reader's V4/V6/V7 links rested on steering accuracy, which does not measure representational alignment, so those labels are dropped. The Qwen3 math rows use hyperparameters grid-searched on dev data. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether representational alignment between independently trained models increases as scale and capability increase, or compare representation-distance similarity across such models.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
Does not compare same-architecture models trained from different random initializations for shared features or subspaces.

Tests linear subspace alignment through downstream capability transfer, but does not directly establish that representations are interchangeable with little loss using stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mappings.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

Examines sensitivity to rank, number of examples, and task/data regime; does not compare alternative representation-similarity metrics or systematically test out-of-distribution representation-distance convergence.
Shows transfer can be incomplete and sensitive to scale and task regime, but does not test whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause alignment.

rows.subject: all tested mapping pairs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured source-to-target hidden-state mapping reconstruction error as the number of examples varied.

conditions.value: n varied; error plateaus at about n≈64

rows.value: Text reports that error improves initially and plateaus as early as n≈64 at very low ranks.
rows.note: Text describes a sample-count effect; exact plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: Reconstruction error of the low-rank linear map does measure map loss, but values are figure-only. Error is averaged over the same n fitting examples (in-sample). Subject should be the three pairs shown: Qwen1.5-14B<-7B, Qwen1.5-7B<-14B, OLMo-2-7B<-1B, at k=4. Not an aggregate over all pairs.

rows.subject: all tested mapping pairs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured source-to-target hidden-state mapping reconstruction error as alignment rank varied.
rows.value: Text reports that increasing rank beyond a threshold degrades performance across models, pronounced beyond k≈128.
rows.note: Text explicitly attributes the higher-rank degradation to overfitting; exact plotted values are figure-only.
rows.check: Figure-only error vs rank at n=512 for the same three pairs. Text says error rises beyond k≈128, which the authors attribute to overfitting. Magnitude of loss not stated in text. This is the method's own fit diagnostic, not a similarity-metric comparison, so not V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported within-family and cross-family reasoning transfers where benchmark accuracy improves
reader_labels.reason: Applying the linearly aligned capability direction improves benchmark accuracy across the listed settings (q15-7-from14-gsm through q3-14-from4-agn-olymp, plus cross-family rows). These are behavioral transfer results, not direct measures of loss in representation alignment.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Weak or negative transfer settings, including gemma-2 large-to-small and some Qwen3 task/benchmark combinations
reader_labels.reason: Transfer gains can be small or absent, and accuracy falls below baseline in several reported conditions (gemma2-2-from9-math; q3-4-from14-cond-minerva; q3-4-from14-agn-agi; q3-4-from14-agn-minerva; q3-14-from4-cond-minerva). The study does not establish near-lossless representational interchangeability from these accuracy outcomes.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Alignment rank and number of examples; task-conditioned versus task-agnostic transfer
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports sample-count saturation at low rank, degradation at higher rank, and different transfer outcomes across task/data regimes and benchmarks (mapping-samples, mapping-rank, and Qwen3 rows).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Transfer direction and model/benchmark conditions reported in the paper
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports directional asymmetry, weak transfer for some smaller or less capable targets, and benchmark-specific losses; these results qualify transfer as incomplete and conditional, without testing the proposed shared-data/objective explanation.
